questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) How bubble sort works (2 marks)**

Bubble sort scans the array from the beginning to the end, comparing each pair of **adjacent** elements and **swapping** them when they are in the wrong order (the first is greater than the second, for an ascending sort). After one pass the largest element has "bubbled" up to the end of the array, which is its final place. The passes are repeated on the part of the array that is not yet sorted, until the array is sorted: at most $n - 1$ passes for $n$ elements, or until a pass is made without any swap.

**(b) Sorting 4, 15, 1, 16, 10 (the number of marks is not printed in the question)**

| Pass | Comparisons and swaps | Content of the array after the pass |
|---|---|---|
| start | | 4, 15, 1, 16, 10 |
| 1 | (4,15) no swap; (15,1) swap; (15,16) no swap; (16,10) swap | 4, 1, 15, 10, 16 |
| 2 | (4,1) swap; (4,15) no swap; (15,10) swap | 1, 4, 10, 15, 16 |
| 3 | (1,4), (4,10), (10,15) no swap at all | 1, 4, 10, 15, 16 |

Pass 3 makes no swap, so the array is sorted and the algorithm stops. The final sorted array is **1, 4, 10, 15, 16**. (An algorithm without a "no swap" test makes a fourth pass, which leaves the array unchanged; the sequence was checked with a Python simulation.)
